input: Hire a personal trainer for three months

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The specific fitness goal (weight loss, muscle gain, rehabilitation, athletic performance) completely changes what kind of trainer to look for and what credentials matter.
Whether training happens at a gym, at home, outdoors, or online determines which trainers are even available and what equipment or space is needed.
Budget per session or per month sets the realistic pool of trainers — rates vary enormously and affect whether to look at boutique studios, big-box gyms, or independent trainers.
How many sessions per week and at what times of day narrows down trainers by availability and determines the total cost of the engagement.
Preferences around the trainer themselves — gender, communication style, coaching approach (tough vs. supportive) — directly affect who to shortlist.
Whether the user wants a highly credentialed specialist (e.g., certified for injury rehab, sports-specific) or a general trainer changes where and how to search.
Knowing what 'a good hire' looks like — verified certifications, trial session, references, a written contract — defines the vetting and decision process.

gold.taskTitle: Hire a personal trainer for three months
gold.taskDescription: Find and engage a personal trainer for a three-month commitment to support the user's fitness goals.

questions.title: What is your primary fitness goal for these three months?
questions.description: Identify the specific outcome the user is training toward — e.g., weight loss, building muscle, injury recovery, sport-specific performance, or general fitness.

questions.title: Where do you want the training sessions to take place?
questions.description: Determine the preferred training environment — a commercial gym, the user's home, outdoors, or fully online/virtual sessions.

questions.title: What is your budget per session or per month?
questions.description: Establish the financial ceiling so the search can be scoped to realistically affordable trainers and settings.

questions.title: How many sessions per week are you aiming for?
questions.description: Clarify training frequency to calculate total cost, assess trainer availability, and build a realistic weekly schedule.

questions.title: Do you have preferences about the trainer's gender or coaching style?
questions.description: Capture any personal preferences — gender, motivational approach (encouraging vs. high-intensity), personality fit — that affect who gets shortlisted.

questions.title: Do you need a trainer with any specialist qualifications?
questions.description: Find out if the user requires expertise in a specific area such as post-injury rehabilitation, pre/postnatal fitness, nutrition coaching, or a particular sport.

questions.title: What would make you confident you have hired the right person?
questions.description: Define the user's vetting criteria — e.g., specific certifications, a trial session, client references, a signed contract, or a satisfaction guarantee.
